We should produce results. Let's compute manually:

gcd(56,98): Euclidean algorithm: 98 mod 56 = 42; 56 mod 42 = 14; 42 mod 14 = 0 => gcd=14.

gcd(81,27) binary algorithm: 81 and 27. Binary GCD algorithm: while both even? 81 odd, 27 odd. If a > b, swap? Actually algorithm: if a==b return a; if a==0 return b; if b==0 return a; if both even, return 2*GCD(a/2,b/2); if a even, return GCD(a/2,b); if b even, return GCD(a,b/2); else if a>b return GCD((a-b)/2,b); else return GCD((b-a)/2,a). Let's compute: a=81,b=27. Both odd, a>b. So compute GCD((81-27)/2=27,27). Now a=27,b=27 => return 27. So gcd=27.

lcm(15,25) standard: lcm = |a*b| / gcd(a,b). gcd(15,25)=5. So lcm=15*25/5=75.

lcm(21,14) reduced algorithm: reduced algorithm likely uses gcd as well but maybe uses reduced method: lcm = a/gcd(a,b)*b. Compute gcd(21,14)=7. Then lcm=21/7*14=3*14=42.

Thus results: gcd(56,98)=14; gcd(81,27)=27; lcm(15,25)=75; lcm(21,14)=42.
